Attester(50/25) is not in the backbone, gets p99 aggregates at `11.17s`, at capacity during aggregates phase and at the start of the next slot due to aggregates tale. 2. Local Block Builder (100/50) is in the backbone, gets p99 aggregates at `8.18s`, not at capacity. 3. `3-4s` to receive attestations and compute an aggregate. If slot is empty, time to aggregate is less but potentially more cores can be used to aggregate cause there is no payload to execute. Fits into LeanVM benches but at capacity in terms of CPU. Potential ways forward: 0. Keep Attester not subscribed to backbone 1. Increase Attester bandwidth 2. Increase CPU requirements / optimize aggregation 3. Reduce number of validators (consolidate) 4. Improve pubsub protocol 5. Increase slot time <@425567222635954178>'s idea on staggered aggregates broadcast: 1) 1st aggregate is published with a *stark* 2) 2nd aggregator observes 1st aggregate and if there are just a few attestations comparing to the 1st aggregate, that aggregator publishes an aggregate with *raw signatures* instead of a stark, and so on for 3rd and other aggregators. This should save us bandwidth in the happy case It's at the cost of verifying a bunch of raw signatures instead of a single stark. Given that we are talking about 100 signatures or something of that size, this should probably be fine Oh this is a variation of what we talked last call, in which the other aggregators don't send anything. I'm skeptical that it is a big improvement though. Say you differ by only 150 signatures (which is very little) then you are already sending the same as another STARK and we are already bottlenecked. I think we need to start testing with the staggered version in which we just don't send anything if we differ by a few signatures Could we add a request / response RPC to fetch attestation aggregates. It this was also advertised by a flag in the ENR, nodes could find peers that can provide aggregates (e.g. nodes on more powerful hardware)? (as a variant on having builders or operators provide aggregates).

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content:
Short summary from recent simulations by <@425567222635954178> :
```
vals=800k, nodes=1k
16 subnets, 2 aggregators, agg_due=6s
att_size=1200 bytes, agg_size=210KiB
gossipsub, D=4

Tier          Nodes  Down / up (Mbit/s)    Vote subnets
Pools           100      10,000 / 10,000             16
VPS             600         500 / 500                 2
Upper home      100         200 / 100                 1
Mid home        100         100 / 50                  1
Home            100          50 / 25                  0
Total         1,000                      
```

Observations:

1. Attester(50/25) is not in the backbone, gets p99 aggregates at `11.17s`, at capacity during aggregates phase and at the start of the next slot due to aggregates tale.
2. Local Block Builder (100/50) is in the backbone, gets p99 aggregates at `8.18s`, not at capacity.
3. `3-4s` to receive attestations and compute an aggregate. If slot is empty, time to aggregate is less but potentially more cores can be used to aggregate cause there is no payload to execute. Fits into LeanVM benches but at capacity in terms of CPU.

Potential ways forward:
0. Keep Attester not subscribed to backbone
1. Increase Attester bandwidth
2. Increase CPU requirements / optimize aggregation
3. Reduce number of validators (consolidate)
4. Improve pubsub protocol
5. Increase slot time

excerpts.author: m.kalinin
excerpts.content:
<@425567222635954178>'s idea on staggered aggregates broadcast:
1) 1st aggregate is published with a *stark*
2) 2nd aggregator observes 1st aggregate and if there are just a few attestations comparing to the 1st aggregate, that aggregator publishes an aggregate with *raw signatures* instead of a stark, and so on for 3rd and other aggregators. This should save us bandwidth in the happy case

It's at the cost of verifying a bunch of raw signatures instead of a single stark. Given that we are talking about 100 signatures or something of that size, this should probably be fine

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: Oh this is a variation of what we talked last call, in which the other aggregators don't send anything. I'm skeptical that it is a big improvement though. Say you differ by only 150 signatures (which is very little) then you are already sending the same as another STARK and we are already bottlenecked. I think we need to start testing with the staggered version in which we just don't send anything if we differ by a few signatures

excerpts.author: vladimir_ea
excerpts.content: Could we add a request / response RPC to fetch attestation aggregates. It this was also advertised by a flag in the ENR, nodes could find peers that can provide aggregates (e.g. nodes on more powerful hardware)? (as a variant on having builders or operators provide aggregates).
